A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 24-page versions of the same TimeSliver paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of all dimensions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and temporal-attribution experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results, including the main experiments and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains identical symbolic encoding, convolutional segment representations, linear aggregation, training objective, and positive/negative attribution procedures.

E1.justification: Both use the same four synthetic attribution datasets, Audio, EEG, FordA, 26 UEA datasets, and the synthetic far-field interaction task in Appendix D.3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main and appendix experiments, including the attribution baselines, UEA classifiers, and Transformer/LSTM/FCN comparison in Table 10.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, model configurations, masking and retraining procedures, and evaluation metrics remain identical in the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the same pooling and activation ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, alternative symbolic representations, far-field interaction test, and qualitative attribution examples.

E5.justification: The three-split/three-trial description in Section 3 and uncertainty reporting in tables and figures are unchanged, including the three-run results in Tables 8 and 10.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted or qualitative findings are identical. For example, both report TimeSliver FreqSum AUPRC of 0.94±0.05 in Table 1 and balanced accuracy of 0.76 with standard deviation 0.02 in Table 10.

T1.justification: Section 2's definitions and equations, Appendix A's scale-invariance argument, and Appendix F's completeness, sensitivity, and symmetry arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims, including 11% attribution improvement across seven datasets and competitive prediction across 26 UEA datasets.

C2.justification: Interpretations of symbolic encoding, attribution behavior, temporal ordering, and component sensitivity are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same proposed human validation and feature-attribution extensions.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical architecture details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, and optimization information. Code-access information is unchanged; the new funding acknowledgment adds no reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions, research positioning, and references are identical. The added NSF acknowledgment does not introduce a cited research work.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5, Acknowledgment, crediting NSF MRSEC support and two NSF grants. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; all other prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment occupies previously blank space below the conclusion on page 10, and page 1's margin stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and remaining page layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding credit in Section 5 and updates its version stamp. This improves administrative completeness, but the scientific content, empirical support, reproducibility information, and explanatory presentation remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
